1.heading: The book of genesis: Abraham to David
1.note: Names from Abraham through Isaac, Jacob and Judah to King David; Tamar, Rahab and Ruth appear as mothers

1.heading: David to exile to Messiah
1.note: Solomon down to Jechoniah at the Babylon exile, then Zerubbabel to Joseph, husband of Mary; fourteen generations counted three times

1.heading: Joseph's crisis and dream
1.note: Mary is found pregnant by the Holy Spirit; Joseph plans to send her away quietly until an angel speaks in a dream

1.heading: Immanuel and Joseph's obedience
1.note: The son is named Immanuel, 'God with us'; Joseph wakes, takes Mary as his wife, and names the child Jesus

2.heading: Magi, Herod, and the Bethlehem citation
2.note: Wise men from the east ask for the newborn King of the Jews; Herod is troubled and sends them to Bethlehem

2.heading: The child receives homage
2.note: The star stops over the house; they fall down and worship, offer gold, frankincense and myrrh, and go home another way after a dream

2.heading: Flight to Egypt and Herod's violence
2.note: An angel sends Joseph fleeing to Egypt by night; Herod kills Bethlehem boys aged two and under; Rachel weeps

2.heading: Return and settlement in Nazareth
2.note: After Herod dies an angel sends Joseph back; afraid of Archelaus, he settles in Nazareth in Galilee

3.heading: John's kingdom announcement
3.note: John in the wilderness wears camel hair and eats locusts and wild honey; crowds come to the Jordan confessing sins

3.heading: Fruit, ancestry, and coming judgment
3.note: John calls the Pharisees and Sadducees 'offspring of vipers'; the ax is at the tree roots, and chaff burns

3.heading: Jesus baptized to fulfill righteousness
3.note: Jesus comes from Galilee to the Jordan; John protests that he needs baptism by Jesus, then allows it

3.heading: Spirit and voice from the heavens
3.note: Coming up from the water, Jesus sees the Spirit descend like a dove; a voice says 'my beloved Son'

4.heading: Bread and the meaning of sonship
4.note: Led into the wilderness, fasting forty days, Jesus is told to make bread; he answers 'Man shall not live by bread alone'

4.heading: Temple spectacle and world rule refused
4.note: On the temple pinnacle he is told to jump; on a high mountain he is offered every kingdom; angels serve him after

4.heading: Light in Galilee and kingdom proclamation
4.note: Jesus withdraws to Galilee, settles in Capernaum by the sea, and begins to preach that the Kingdom of Heaven is at hand

4.heading: Fishermen called; teaching, preaching, healing
4.note: Simon, Andrew, James and John leave nets and boat to follow him; then he teaches and heals, and crowds follow

5.heading: Beatitudes: who is called fortunate
5.note: On the mountain he teaches disciples blessings for mourners, the gentle, the merciful, peacemakers and the persecuted; 'great is your reward'

5.heading: Salt, light, and visible good
5.note: 'You are the salt of the earth' and the light of the world; a hill city and a lamp on a stand

5.heading: Law, fulfillment, and greater righteousness
5.note: He came to fulfill the law, not destroy it; not a pen stroke passes; righteousness must exceed the scribes and Pharisees

5.heading: Anger, desire, divorce, and oaths
5.note: Murder, lust, divorce and oaths each get 'But I tell you'; make peace before the altar; pluck out the eye

5.heading: Nonretaliation and enemy love
5.note: Turn the other cheek, give the cloak, walk the second mile, love enemies; the Father sends rain on just and unjust

6.heading: Giving, praying, and fasting before the Father
6.note: Give, pray and fast in secret, not like hypocrites; a prayer begins 'Our Father in heaven' and asks daily bread, forgiven debts

6.heading: Treasure, eye, and two masters
6.note: Treasure on earth falls to moth, rust and thieves; the eye is the lamp of the body; no one can serve God and Mammon

6.heading: Anxiety, creation, and first seeking
6.note: Look at the birds and the lilies; stop worrying about food and clothes, seek the Kingdom first, and leave tomorrow alone

7.heading: Judgment, self-examination, and discernment
7.note: The measure you use is used on you; a speck in a brother's eye, a beam in yours; no pearls for pigs

7.heading: Ask, seek, knock, and the Father's goodness
7.note: Ask, seek, knock; a son asking for bread is not given a stone; do to others what you want done to you

7.heading: Two ways and false prophets
7.note: A narrow gate leads to life, a wide gate to destruction; wolves in sheep's clothing are known by fruit; bad trees burn

7.heading: Profession, practice, and two foundations
7.note: Saying 'Lord, Lord' is not enough; the house on rock stands in flood, the house on sand falls; crowds are astonished

8.heading: Cleansing by touch and healing by a word
8.note: A leper says 'if you want to' and Jesus touches him; a centurion asks help for his paralyzed servant; a word heals

8.heading: Household and crowd restored; Isaiah fulfilled
8.note: Peter's mother-in-law has a fever that leaves at a touch, and she serves; at evening he casts out spirits and heals all

8.heading: The cost of crossing with Jesus
8.note: A scribe offers to follow anywhere; the Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head; another wants to bury his father

8.heading: Storm, little faith, and authority over demons
8.note: He sleeps through a storm, then rebukes the sea; demons enter pigs that rush down the cliff; the city begs him to leave

9.heading: Forgiveness made visible in healing
9.note: Men bring a paralyzed man on a bed; Jesus says his sins are forgiven, then tells him to take his mat home

9.heading: Matthew's table and mercy over sacrifice
9.note: Jesus says 'Follow me' to Matthew at the tax office; tax collectors and sinners eat with them; the sick need a physician

9.heading: Bridegroom, cloth, and new wine
9.note: Asked about fasting, Jesus speaks of the bridegroom, a cloth patch on an old garment, and new wine in old wineskins

9.heading: A daughter and a hemorrhaging woman
9.note: A ruler says his daughter just died; a woman bleeding twelve years touches his fringe; the girl arises

9.heading: Sight, speech, controversy, and compassion
9.note: Two blind men see and a mute man speaks; Pharisees blame the prince of demons; Jesus pities crowds like shepherdless sheep

10.heading: The Twelve named and authorized
10.note: He calls twelve disciples and gives authority over unclean spirits and disease; the names run from Simon Peter to Judas Iscariot

10.heading: Israel-focused journey and dependent hospitality
10.note: Sent to the lost sheep of Israel, not Gentiles or Samaritans; no gold or bag; shake the dust off if refused

10.heading: Sheep among wolves and Spirit-given witness
10.note: Sheep among wolves, scourged in synagogues, brought before governors; 'it is not you who speak'; a disciple is not above his teacher

10.heading: Fear God, confess openly, carry the cross
10.note: Do not fear those who kill the body; sparrows, numbered hairs; confess or be denied; a sword, not peace; take your cross

10.heading: Receiving the messenger and the sender
10.note: Whoever receives you receives him and the one who sent him; a prophet's reward; even a cup of cold water counts

11.heading: John's question and Jesus's Isaianic answer
11.note: John in prison sends disciples asking 'Are you he who comes'; Jesus answers: the blind see, lepers are cleansed, the dead rise

11.heading: John's greatness and the difficult kingdom saying
11.note: Reed, soft clothing, prophet: what did they go out to see?; John is 'Elijah, who is to come'

11.heading: A generation refusing both funeral and dance
11.note: Children in the marketplace say flute and mourning got no answer; John 'has a demon', the Son of Man is called a drunkard

11.heading: Unresponsive towns and greater accountability
11.note: Woe to Chorazin and Bethsaida; Capernaum will go down to Hades; Tyre, Sidon and Sodom will find judgment 'more tolerable'

11.heading: Revelation, yoke, and rest
11.note: Jesus thanks the Father for revealing things to infants; 'Come to me' all who are heavily burdened; his yoke is easy

12.heading: Grain, Sabbath, and mercy
12.note: Hungry disciples pluck grain on the Sabbath; Jesus cites David and the show bread: 'one greater than the temple is here'

12.heading: Healing and the servant who does not crush
12.note: A man with a withered hand is healed in the synagogue; Pharisees plot; the chosen servant will not 'break a bruised reed'

12.heading: Spirit, divided kingdom, and decisive allegiance
12.note: Pharisees say he casts out demons by Beelzebul; Jesus answers 'divided against itself', speaks of binding the strong man, warns about idle words

12.heading: Jonah, return of the spirit, and Jesus's family
12.note: Asked for a sign, he offers only Jonah; an unclean spirit returns with seven worse; disciples are 'my mother and my brothers'

13.heading: Sower, purpose of parables, and four soils
13.note: From a boat he tells of seed on road, rock, thorns and good soil; then explains why parables, and each soil

13.heading: Wheat and weeds; mustard and yeast
13.note: An enemy sows weeds among wheat and both grow to harvest; a mustard seed becomes a tree; yeast works through the meal

13.heading: Explanation of the weeds
13.note: In the house he explains the weeds: field is the world, enemy the devil, reapers angels; the righteous 'shine like the sun'

13.heading: Treasure, pearl, net, and disciple-scribe
13.note: A man sells all for a hidden treasure, a merchant for one pearl; a dragnet sorts fish; a scribe brings out new and old

13.heading: A prophet without honor at home
13.note: In his own country they are astonished, then offended, naming his mother Mary and brothers; he does few mighty works there

14.heading: Herod's feast and John's death
14.note: Herod thinks Jesus is John risen; the daughter of Herodias dances, Herod swears an oath, and John is beheaded in prison

14.heading: Compassion and bread in a deserted place
14.note: Crowds follow on foot and he heals their sick; 'You give them something to eat'; five loaves, two fish, twelve baskets left

14.heading: Jesus and Peter on the sea
14.note: Jesus walks on the sea in the fourth watch; Peter steps out, sinks, and cries 'Lord, save me'; those in the boat worship him

14.heading: Recognition and healing at Gennesaret
14.note: At Gennesaret people recognize him and bring all the sick; everyone who touches the fringe of his garment is made whole

15.heading: Tradition, command, lips, and heart
15.note: Asked about unwashed hands, Jesus answers with 'Honor your father and your mother' and calls them hypocrites whose hearts are far away

15.heading: Defilement redefined and explained
15.note: What 'proceeds out of the mouth' defiles; blind guides fall into a pit; evil thoughts come from the heart, not unwashed hands

15.heading: The Canaanite woman's persistent faith
15.note: A Canaanite woman begs help for her daughter; he is silent, then speaks of dogs; she answers with crumbs, and her daughter is healed

15.heading: Healing and feeding four thousand
15.note: By the sea he heals the lame, blind and mute; seven loaves and a few small fish feed four thousand men

16.heading: A demanded sign and the yeast misunderstood
16.note: Pharisees and Sadducees ask for a sign and get only Jonah; the disciples forgot bread and hear 'beware of the yeast'

16.heading: Peter's confession and Jesus's promises
16.note: At Caesarea Philippi Peter says 'the Son of the living God'; Jesus names him Peter, speaks of a rock and keys

16.heading: The suffering Messiah and Satanic resistance
16.note: Jesus says he must go to Jerusalem, suffer, be killed and raised; Peter rebukes him and hears 'Get behind me, Satan'

16.heading: Cross-bearing, life, and the Son of Man's coming
16.note: Deny himself and take up his cross; whoever loses life for Jesus finds it; what profit if he 'gains the whole world'

17.heading: Transfiguration and the voice: listen to the Son
17.note: His face shines like the sun on a mountain; Moses and Elijah appear; Peter offers tents; a voice from the cloud says 'Listen to him'

17.heading: Elijah, John, and suffering
17.note: Told to keep silent until the Son of Man rises, they ask about Elijah; Jesus says he has come, meaning John

17.heading: Failed exorcism, little faith, and mustard seed
17.note: A father says the disciples could not cure his son; Jesus rebukes the demon; faith like a mustard seed moves a mountain

17.heading: Betrayal predicted and temple tax paid freely
17.note: He again says the Son of Man will be killed and raised; asked about the tax, he sends Peter to find a coin in a fish's mouth

18.heading: A child in the middle and true greatness
18.note: Asked who is greatest, Jesus sets a child in the middle: unless you 'become as little children' you will not enter

18.heading: Stumbling, self-judgment, and little ones
18.note: A millstone is better than causing little ones to stumble; cut off the hand or foot; a man seeks one lost sheep

18.heading: A process for regaining a sibling
18.note: If a brother sins, go alone, then take one or two, then tell the assembly; 'where two or three are gathered'

18.heading: Seventy-sevenfold forgiveness and refused mercy
18.note: Peter proposes seven times; Jesus says 'seventy times seven'; a servant forgiven ten thousand talents jails a debtor of a hundred denarii

19.heading: Divorce tested against creation fidelity
19.note: Pharisees ask about divorce for any reason; Jesus cites male and female, 'one flesh', and says Moses allowed it for hard hearts

19.heading: Marriage, celibacy, and capacity to receive
19.note: Disciples say it is better not to marry; Jesus says not all can receive this, and speaks of three kinds of eunuchs

19.heading: Children welcomed into the kingdom
19.note: Children are brought for prayer and the disciples rebuke them; Jesus says the Kingdom 'belongs to ones like these'

19.heading: The wealthy seeker and impossible salvation
19.note: A rich young man is told to sell all and follow; he leaves sad; 'with God all things are possible'

19.heading: Renewal, relinquishment, and last becoming first
19.note: Peter asks what they get for leaving everything; twelve thrones, a hundred times as much; 'many will be last who are first'

20.heading: Workers, a denarius, and the owner's generosity
20.note: A master hires workers at dawn and later hours, then pays all a denarius; the first grumble; 'the last will be first'

20.heading: The third and most detailed passion prediction
20.note: Going up to Jerusalem he says the Son of Man will be condemned, mocked, scourged, crucified, and raised the third day

20.heading: Royal seats, the cup, service, and ransom
20.note: A mother asks seats for her sons; the ten are indignant; he gives his life 'a ransom for many'

20.heading: Two silenced men receive sight and follow
20.note: Two blind men by the road cry out for mercy and are told to be quiet; Jesus touches their eyes; they follow

21.heading: Humble king enters to Hosanna
21.note: Two disciples fetch a donkey and colt; crowds spread clothes and branches and cry 'Hosanna to the son of David'

21.heading: Temple protest, healing, and children's praise
21.note: He drives out sellers, overturns tables, and calls the temple 'a den of robbers'; he heals the lame and blind

21.heading: Fig tree, faith, and prayer
21.note: Hungry, he finds only leaves on a fig tree and it withers; he says faith can throw a mountain into the sea

21.heading: Authority and the two sons
21.note: Asked his authority, Jesus asks about the baptism of John; they will not answer. Of two sons, the one who refused goes

21.heading: Violent tenants and the rejected stone
21.note: Tenant farmers beat and kill the servants, then the son; Jesus cites the rejected stone; the chief priests see it targets them

22.heading: Wedding invitation refused and the unready guest
22.note: Invited guests refuse a king's wedding feast and kill his servants; strangers fill it; a man without wedding clothing is thrown out

22.heading: Caesar's coin and God's claim
22.note: Asked about taxes to Caesar, Jesus asks for the tax coin and whose image it bears; give Caesar and God their own

22.heading: Sadducees, marriage, and resurrection
22.note: Sadducees pose seven brothers and one widow; Jesus says none marry in the resurrection; God is 'not the God of the dead'

22.heading: Love of God and neighbor
22.note: A lawyer asks the greatest commandment; Jesus answers 'love the Lord your God', then your neighbor as yourself

22.heading: David's son and David's Lord
22.note: Jesus asks whose son the Christ is; they say 'Of David'; how then does David call him Lord? No one answers

23.heading: Moses's seat, heavy burdens, and performed status
23.note: Scribes and Pharisees sit on the seat of Moses; they bind heavy burdens and love the best seats; call no one father

23.heading: Woes: blocking, exploiting, and corrupted guidance
23.note: Woes on hypocrites who shut the Kingdom, devour widows' houses and chase one convert; oaths by temple gold and altar gifts

23.heading: Weightier matters and clean insides
23.note: They tithe mint, dill and cumin but skip justice, mercy and faith; strain out a gnat and 'swallow a camel'; whitened tombs

23.heading: Prophetic blood, accountability, and lament
23.note: They build tombs for prophets yet are 'children of those who killed the prophets'; Jerusalem is like a hen gathering chicks

24.heading: Temple prediction and protection against deception
24.note: Disciples show him the temple; no stone will stay on another; on the Mount of Olives he lists false Christs and wars

24.heading: Desolating sacrilege, flight, and tribulation
24.note: At the abomination of desolation, flee to the mountains; great suffering; false christs show signs; the Son of Man comes like lightning

24.heading: Cosmic signs and the Son of Man
24.note: After those days the sun darkens and stars fall; the Son of Man comes on the clouds, and angels gather the chosen

24.heading: Fig tree, this generation, and enduring words
24.note: The fig tree's leaves show summer is near; 'this generation will not pass away'; 'my words will not pass away'

24.heading: Unknown day and faithful readiness
24.note: No one knows the day, not even angels; the days of Noah; two in a field, one taken; a thief; two servants

25.heading: Ten young women and delayed readiness
25.note: Ten virgins take lamps to meet the bridegroom; five foolish ones have no oil at midnight, and the door is shut

25.heading: Entrusted wealth, faithful risk, and fearful burial
25.note: A man leaves five, two and one talents with servants; two double theirs and hear 'Well done'; the third buries his

25.heading: The Son of Man judges nations through the least
25.note: The King sets sheep on his right and goats on his left; fed, clothed and visited 'the least of these', or not

26.heading: Plot, anointing, and betrayal price
26.note: Chief priests plot in the court of Caiaphas; a woman pours costly ointment on his head; Judas takes thirty silver pieces

26.heading: Passover, betrayer, bread, and covenant cup
26.note: At the Passover meal he says one will betray him; bread is 'my body', the cup 'blood of the new covenant'

26.heading: Scattering predicted and Gethsemane prayer
26.note: Peter will deny him; in Gethsemane he prays 'let this cup pass away'; the disciples sleep

26.heading: Betrayal, arrest, and disciples' flight
26.note: Judas identifies him with a kiss; a sword cuts off the ear of the high priest's servant; the disciples flee

26.heading: Jesus before the council; Peter in the courtyard
26.note: Before Caiaphas two false witnesses speak of the temple; the high priest tears his clothing; Peter denies him three times and weeps

27.heading: Judas, innocent blood, and the potter's field
27.note: Judas returns the thirty silver pieces, saying 'innocent blood', and hangs himself; the priests buy the potter's field for strangers

27.heading: Pilate, Barabbas, crowd, and handwashing
27.note: Jesus answers Pilate 'So you say' then stays silent; the crowd picks Barabbas; Pilate washes his hands; Jesus is flogged

27.heading: Mocked king led to crucifixion
27.note: Soldiers dress him in scarlet and thorns and mock 'Hail, King of the Jews'; Simon of Cyrene carries the cross to Golgotha

27.heading: Cry, death, torn veil, quake, and confession
27.note: Darkness falls; he cries 'My God, my God' and dies; the veil tears, tombs open, the centurion confesses 'Son of God'

27.heading: Joseph's tomb and the guard
27.note: Joseph of Arimathaea asks Pilate for the body and lays it in his new tomb; priests set a guard, seal the stone

28.heading: Women, earthquake, angel, and empty tomb
28.note: Two women come at dawn; an earthquake, an angel rolls the stone, guards fall like dead men; 'He is not here'

28.heading: Jesus meets and sends the women
28.note: Jesus meets the women on their way; they hold his feet and worship; he tells them to send his brothers to Galilee

28.heading: The guards' report and a purchased counter-story
28.note: The guards tell the chief priests what happened; the elders give them silver to say the disciples stole the body

28.heading: Worship, doubt, all authority, and all nations
28.note: On a Galilee mountain the eleven bow, though some doubted; Jesus says 'All authority has been given to me'

limits: The sources are old reference works (Thayer's, Strong's, Whiston's Josephus), the Mishnah in Sefaria's English, and Wikipedia. They show a claim is standard; they are not current scholarship.

The reviewers' source quotations came through a page reader that returns short excerpts. The lead re-checked four of them (Josephus, Antiquities 17.8.1 and 18.1.4; Mishnah Gittin 9:10; the hosted Didache 7:1) and read every proposed edit and outline note. The other quotations were not re-read.
Each reviewer was one pass over seven chapters with a stated bar ("a careful editor would ask: says who?"). A claim below that bar may remain.

The 82 claims marked `text` rest on the hosted World English Bible or the site's tagged Greek. Where the hosted English follows a different Greek reading from the tagged edition (3:11, 6:1, 11:19, 24:36), the guide now says so.
Readings marked as readings were not adjudicated.
The drafter of these guides is not recorded. Commit 52b2d572 of 2026-08-04, which rewrote all 28, names no model.
